Kamikaze survivors debunk stereotype in stories of sacrifice

Good article. But the title is a click-bait. What exactly is the "stereotype" they are debunking? It's obvious that human beings don't want to die (survival instinct is wired into us by natural selection), and I would imagine most kamikazes didn't. The fact that kamikazes were a mix of legitimate volunteers and "semi-volunteers" is also known -- when offered to die gloriously for the Emperor, almost all Japanese of the day would choose death, mostly out of fear of appearing cowardly.

If anyone wants to learn a bit more about the peculiar Japanese "culture of shame", I would suggest the book "The Chrysanthemum and the Sword". It's old, but it's still one of the best books on the subject.
